commentary_title: VLCC utilisation strengthens despite weaker tonne-mile demand
commentary_summary: VLCC utilisation rose to 93.7% in Week 43, up 2.5 percentage points MoM and YoY, indicating significantly tighter fleet employment. However, the tonne-mile index remained subdued at 91.7, down 17.4% YoY, suggesting that shorter-haul crude movements and weaker long-haul trade flows continue to weigh on underlying transport demand despite the recent recovery from mid-year lows. | Higher fleet employment was driven by stronger vessel deployment, with the share of laden vessels declining by 1.6 percentage points MoM in the East and 3.3 percentage points in the West, while the proportion of vessels underway increased and in-port tonnage fell sharply. At the same time, anchored capacity declined by 46.0% MoM in the West and 1.5% in the East, indicating improved vessel circulation and reduced congestion across key trading regions. | Market tightness remained broadly balanced as stronger utilisation was partially offset by improving fleet productivity. Ballast speeds increased by 6.2% MoM in the East and 8.1% in the West despite bunker prices rising 8.6% MoM to $933/tonne, while laden anchor days increased 3.2% on a four-week moving-average basis.
